title: Poulet au Vinaigre
subtitle: Lyonnaise chicken braised in red wine vinegar with tomato and tarragon
excerpt: Bone-in chicken thighs are browned and then braised in red wine vinegar, tomatoes, and stock until the sauce reduces to something tangy, rich, and completely un-sharp. A Lyonnaise bistro classic that takes under an hour.
sourceNotes: Lyonnaise bistro classic. Synthesised from the traditional recipe associated with the bouchon kitchens of Lyon.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the braise without cream. Add cream when reheating gently on the hob.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Use a wide pan so all the chicken can brown without crowding.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The braise improves overnight. Reheat gently and add the cream just before serving.

content.text: The vinegar cooks out completely and leaves a rounded, slightly sharp sauce with real depth. Use bone-in thighs for the best result. Boneless thighs work but give a thinner sauce.
Pat the chicken thighs dry with kitchen paper. Season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Heat the butter and olive oil in the frying pan over a medium-high heat. Brown the chicken skin-side down for 5 to 6 minutes until deep golden. Flip and cook for 3 minutes more. Remove and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Cook the shallots in the same pan for 4 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Pour in the red wine vinegar. Let it bubble hard for 3 minutes, scraping the base of the pan. The sharp smell will soften as it reduces.
Add the tinned tomatoes and stock. Bring to a simmer and stir. Nestle the chicken back in, skin-side up.
Simmer uncovered for 25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has thickened. The liquid should reduce by about a third.
Stir in the creme fraiche and most of the tarragon. Taste for salt. Simmer for 2 minutes. Rest for 5 minutes before serving with the remaining tarragon scattered over.

items.symptom: The sauce is still very acidic after cooking.
items.cause: The vinegar did not reduce long enough before the stock was added.
items.fix: Simmer the finished dish without the lid for 5 more minutes to mellow it further.

items.symptom: The sauce is thin and watery.
items.cause: Too much stock was used or the heat was too low to reduce properly.
items.fix: Remove the chicken and boil the sauce hard for 5 minutes until it coats a spoon.

items.symptom: The chicken skin is soft rather than browned.
items.cause: The pan was not hot enough at the start, or the skin was wet.
items.fix: Pat chicken very dry before browning and make sure the pan is properly hot before the chicken goes in.
